decisions.rationale: "Duchenne muscular dystrophy" is used as a modifier of the noun "gene" ("murine Duchenne muscular dystrophy gene"), so it is annotated as a Modifier rather than a standalone Specific Disease.
"Duchenne muscular dystrophy" modifies the noun phrase "messenger RNA" (Dmd messenger RNA), so it is a disease name used as a Modifier.
"Dmd" here is the gene symbol in parentheses naming the gene and its mRNA, not a disease mention, so it is not annotated.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate (only disease mentions are in scope; gene symbols are non-disease referents)

decisions.rationale: "Dmd mRNA" refers to the gene transcript, not to a disease, so it is not annotated.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate (only disease mentions are in scope; gene symbols are non-disease referents)

decisions.rationale: "Dmd mRNA" refers to the gene transcript in brain and muscle, not to a disease, so it is not annotated.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate (only disease mentions are in scope; gene symbols are non-disease referents)

decisions.rationale: "dystrophic" describes the mice as having a muscular dystrophy condition and modifies the noun "mice"; it is a disease-derived term used as a modifier.
"mdx" is a mouse mutant strain or allele designation rather than a disease name, so it is not annotated.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate (only disease mentions are in scope; strain and mutation designations are non-disease referents)

decisions.rationale: "Dmd gene mutations" refers to the mouse gene and its mutations, not to a disease, so it is not annotated.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate (only disease mentions are in scope; gene symbols are non-disease referents)

decisions.rationale: "Duchenne muscular dystrophy" modifies the noun "gene expression" (human Duchenne muscular dystrophy gene expression), so it is a disease name used as a Modifier.
"DMD" is the abbreviation of Duchenne muscular dystrophy, annotated as a separate synonymous mention, and it modifies the noun "gene expression".
"mental retardation" is a broad family of heterogeneous conditions rather than one specific disease, matching the grey-area example that is annotated as Disease Class.
